text.p: These are the leading stories in the Beirut press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-The new parliamet is complete; one of its most important tasks would be to pass a new elections law and to elect a new president when President Hrawi's term expires in 1998.
-Hrawi said as he cast his vote on Sunday in the last rounds of Lebanon's five-round general election: "The Lebanese have the right to form coalitions".
-Voting in force in the last hour in the Bekaa raised turnout to 52 percent, the hightest of all five-stages of the elections.
-Interior Minister Murr said the polls ended without any security problems and the total turnout in Lebanon in all five stages is 66 percent.
-Christians in Zahle crossed out the names of Hizbollah candidates or allies on the election lists.
-Foreign Minister Bouez informs Egyptian President Mubarak in Cairo about Israeli threats to Lebanon.
-A small explosion in a Sidon home kills one person and wound two.
-Violations cited during the Bekaa valley vote; reports of 35,000 identity cards lost from Zahle serai but the interior ministry denies it.
-President Hrawi: "If the elections were not held on their due date, Lebanon would have lost international trust in it".
-The Lebanese Association for the Democracy of Elections says electroal breaches in the Bekaa valley were similar to those in other areas during earlier rounds of voting.
